intro: A Detroit producer and MC with his live band.
story: Black Milk is Curtis Cross, a Detroit rapper and producer who has made beats for Slum Village, Danny Brown and others and tours with the live band Nat Turner. The Rebellion Sessions, a live instrumental album with the band, came out in 2016, the year before their Pickathon set. FEVER followed on Mass Appeal on February 23, 2018, and The Guardian heard gorgeous beats carrying more of a story. In 2025 he released the solo album Food From the Gods.
artist_reel_line: FEVER came out on Mass Appeal on February 23, 2018.

intro: A Portland psych-pop songwriter with reverb-soaked songs.
story: Cat Hoch is a Portland multi-instrumentalist who leads a psychedelic dream-pop band, and Willamette Week named her to its Best New Bands of 2016. The EP Look What You Found came out in October 2015, recorded at The Green House in Northeast Portland. She played Pickathon in 2017. Her debut LP, Temptations, produced by Riley Geare, arrived on Amplus Records in 2019, with a release show on September 29 at Music Millennium.
artist_reel_line: Temptations, her debut LP, came out on Amplus Records in 2019.

intro: A Portland drummer, singer and producer.
story: Coco Columbia grew up in Bend studying jazz drumming, and left jazz programs at the University of Oregon and Portland State to write songs. She has said she listened to rock, punk and metal early, jazz in high school, then soul, R&B and hip-hop in college. She wears a blue wig onstage. In March 2017 she placed ninth in Willamette Week's Best New Band poll, and that summer she played Pickathon.
artist_reel_line: She placed ninth in Willamette Week's Best New Band poll in March 2017.

story: Ex-Cult began in Memphis as Sex Cult and changed the name after a cease-and-desist letter. Ty Segall heard them at SXSW and produced their 2012 debut. Midnight Passenger came out on Goner on April 29, 2014, recorded by Doug Easley, and PopMatters praised it for sharpening the band's claws without mistaking loud for noisy. Singer Chris Shaw formed GØGGS with Segall and Charlie Moothart, and Castle Face released their Cigarette Machine EP in 2015. Negative Growth, on In the Red, followed in 2016, and the band played Pickathon in 2017.
artist_reel_line: Negative Growth, on In the Red, was their 2016 album.

intro: A funk-jazz collective from the Snarky Puppy circle.
story: Ghost-Note is a Dallas percussion-led funk and jazz group founded in 2015 by two members of Snarky Puppy, Robert Sput Searight and Nate Werth. They played Pickathon in 2017. Mustard n' Onions, a 15-track double album with guests including Marcus Miller, came out on Mack Avenue in 2024, and in November 2025 NPR posted a Ghost-Note Tiny Desk concert.
artist_reel_line: NPR posted a Ghost-Note Tiny Desk concert in November 2025.

intro: A young Maryland soul singer before his debut album.
story: Jalen Ngonda was born near Washington, D.C., and later settled in London and Liverpool. He played Pickathon in 2017, six years before his debut. Come Around and Love Me came out on Daptone Records in 2023, and Bandcamp Daily's Album of the Day review praised how it draws on R&B greats. A second album, Doctrine of Love, followed in 2026.

intro: A Los Angeles R&B trio of lush harmonies.
story: KING is a Los Angeles trio of the Minneapolis-raised twin sisters Amber and Paris Strother and Anita Bias; Prince invited the sisters to open his 21-night Forum run. Their EP The Story came out in 2011, and the debut We Are KING in February 2016, self-produced and self-released. NPR's First Listen said KING excels at setting a mood, and Stereogum made it Album of the Week. They played Pickathon in 2017.

intro: A Colombian collective in New York with brass and percussion.
story: M.A.K.U. Soundsystem is a New York band, most of whose members come from Colombia, formed in 2010, and its first album, Vamos Bien, was tied to a summer 2010 show at Lincoln Center Out of Doors. They have since played SXSW and GlobalFEST. Mezcla, on Glitterbeat Records, came out in 2016, and the band played Pickathon the next summer.
artist_reel_line: Mezcla, on Glitterbeat Records, came out in 2016.

intro: A North Portland rapper with local-rooted lyrics.
story: Mic Capes is a rapper from St. Johns in North Portland who started recording in 2012, and Willamette Week named him rapper of the year in 2015. He has said his music speaks to people from poverty and low-income backgrounds, and he wants to inspire inner-city kids. Rise and Grind came out in 2012, Concrete Dreams in 2016 and Sheesh, with the producer Drae Slapz, in 2017, the year of his Pickathon set. In 2026 he released SHEESH II: With All Due Respect... and the single Jurassic Park.

intro: A Portland soul singer with rich vocal harmonies.
story: Moorea Masa learned to sing in a gospel church in Portland, and has recorded with the Decemberists and toured as a backup singer for k.d. lang and Ural Thomas. She played Pickathon in 2017 with her band The Mood. Their debut full-length, Shine a Light, came out on May 11, 2018.
artist_reel_line: Shine a Light, with The Mood, came out on May 11, 2018.

intro: A Portland roots-rock band fronted by two brothers.
story: Quiet Life is a roots-rock band built on the brothers Sean and Ryan Spellman, who toured in a van converted to run on used cooking oil. Wild Pack, produced in Portland by Adam Selzer, followed their 2011 album Big Green. They played Pickathon in 2017, and have been quiet in recent years.

intro: A soulful songwriter of blues and gospel, then new.
story: Ron Artis II grew up in Hawai'i as the eldest of 11 siblings who all make music, and played in the Artis Family Band as a kid. His album What Music Means to Me came out in 2015, and he played Pickathon in 2017. Soul Street followed on April 6, 2018.
artist_reel_line: Soul Street came out on April 6, 2018.

intro: A Portland R&B singer of smooth, late-night vocals.
story: TYuS is the Portland R&B singer TYuS Strickland, who produces his own music and signed a major-label deal. He played Pickathon in 2017. His most recent releases have been singles in 2023 and 2024.

intro: A Portland roots-country band with an earthy sound.
story: The Desert Kind is the Portland project of the songwriter Chris Bigley, begun in 2014 with a roots-minimalist sound in the vein of Shovels and Rope and Shakey Graves. Their Bad Wolf EP came out in March 2017, and they played Pickathon that summer.

intro: A British folk-psych quartet of heavy, pastoral riffs.
story: Wolf People came back to Pickathon in 2017, two years after their first visit, with Ruins, on Jagjaguwar, from 2016. Jack Sharp formed the band in Bedford, England, in 2005, and Fain, in April 2013, followed the 2010 debut Steeple, which was recorded at guitarist Joe Hollick's house in Yorkshire. Spectrum Culture called them heirs to Fairport Convention and Steeleye Span. They announced an indefinite hiatus in January 2020.

intro: A genre-bending soul and punk singer.
story: Xenia Rubinos is a Brooklyn singer-songwriter with a Puerto Rican mother and a Cuban father and a jazz composition degree from Berklee. Black Terry Cat, her second album after the 2013 debut Magic Trix, came out on Anti- on June 3, 2016, and NPR's Alt.Latino reviewed it. She played Pickathon in 2017. Una Rosa followed on Anti- on October 15, 2021, and Stereogum made it Album of the Week.

intro: A Portland band led by Luz Elena Mendoza.
story: Luz Elena Mendoza was born in San Francisco to immigrants from Michoacan, Mexico, and raised in Southern Oregon; she formed Y La Bamba in Portland around 2008. They played Pickathon in 2012 and returned in 2017. Mujeres, the first album she produced herself, came out on Tender Loving Empire in February 2019, and Paste called it the band's most uncompromising. The bilingual EP Entre Los Dos followed in September 2019, and Lucha in 2023. Mendoza has said she moved to Guadalajara at 37, and it feels more like home than ever.
